name: Combination Sweeper-Scrubber
definition: A commercial ride-on cleaning machine with a documented dry sweeping system and debris hopper plus a wet scrubbing, squeegee and recovery system integrated on the same platform.
includedScope: Integrated machines that sweep debris and scrub hard floors in one platform
Battery or engine-powered ride-on combination machines
excludedScope: Two separate machines sold as a package
Road sweepers without wet scrubbing and recovery
Ordinary scrubbers with only a light pre-sweep accessory
Machines without a documented debris hopper
headline: Combination sweeper-scrubber architecture, hopper, dust control, wet recovery and buyer verification
description: This profile separates the dry sweeping and wet scrubbing subsystems, explains one-pass claim boundaries, and gives buyers a route, debris, utility and service verification framework.
metaDescription: Combination sweeper-scrubber guide covering sweeping, hopper, dust control, scrubbing, recovery, models and buyer checks.
disclaimer: This independent category reference is not model-specific purchasing, safety, dust-hazard, chemical or repair advice. Confirm the exact machine, powertrain, filters, floor, debris, regional conformity and service terms.

keyFacts.label: Architecture boundary
keyFacts.value: Full dry sweeping and hopper plus full wet scrubbing and recovery on one chassis
keyFacts.evidence: Official category and model sources explicitly describe integrated sweeping and scrubbing systems.
keyFacts.scope: Reviewed combination machines; no inference from a side brush alone.

keyFacts.label: One-pass boundary
keyFacts.value: One platform can sweep and scrub, but achieved one-pass results remain debris- and site-dependent
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturers state integrated or one-pass operation while manuals define operating limits.

keyFacts.label: Dust boundary
keyFacts.value: Sweep filtration and dust suppression are separate from wet recovery
keyFacts.evidence: Official sources identify sweep filters, shakers or dust systems separately from scrub tanks and squeegees.

keyFacts.label: Powertrain boundary
keyFacts.value: Battery, diesel, LPG and gasoline configurations have different indoor-use and utility implications
keyFacts.evidence: Manufacturer pages publish model-specific power options.

systemFlow.name: Debris capture
systemFlow.componentFamily: Side brooms and main sweeping brush
systemFlow.role: Moves loose debris into the sweep chamber.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources identify side and main sweeping brushes.
systemFlow.scope: Brush type and path are configuration-specific.

systemFlow.name: Hopper loading
systemFlow.componentFamily: Sweep chamber, conveyor or overthrow path and debris hopper
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers publish hopper systems and capacities.
systemFlow.scope: Usable capacity depends on debris density and fill limits.

systemFlow.name: Dust management
systemFlow.role: Controls airborne dust created during dry sweeping.
systemFlow.evidence: Official pages list sweep filters and dust-control features.

systemFlow.name: Wet scrubbing
systemFlow.componentFamily: Solution tank, dosing and scrub deck
systemFlow.role: Applies liquid and agitation after or with debris pickup.
systemFlow.evidence: Official sources document solution capacities and scrub systems.

systemFlow.name: Liquid recovery
systemFlow.componentFamily: Squeegee, vacuum path and recovery tank
systemFlow.role: Collects dirty solution and stores it for draining.
systemFlow.evidence: Manufacturers publish recovery systems and tank data.
systemFlow.scope: Turns, floor joints and blade condition affect result.

variants.name: Battery compact combination machine
variants.operatorRelationship: Ride-on operator manages debris, water and charging
variants.spaceConstraints: Turning circle, doorway and charging area are critical
variants.limitations: Compactness can reduce tank and hopper capacity.
variants.evidence: Nilfisk positions CS7500 as compact and battery-powered.

variants.name: Large battery industrial machine
variants.operatorRelationship: Ride-on operator with hydraulic hopper handling
variants.spaceConstraints: Requires substantial turn, transport and service clearance
variants.limitations: Nominal productivity excludes dumps, fills and edge work.
variants.evidence: Tennant M17 and Hako B400 sources document large battery platforms.

variants.name: Engine-powered combination machine
variants.taskScale: Heavy indoor/outdoor industrial work where approved
variants.operatorRelationship: Ride-on operator manages fuel, exhaust and additional maintenance
variants.spaceConstraints: Ventilation, emissions, noise and fuel storage govern use
variants.limitations: Engine availability does not establish indoor authorization.
variants.evidence: Tennant M20 and Nilfisk CS7010 publish engine configurations.

performanceMetrics.name: Sweeping and scrubbing paths
performanceMetrics.purchasingMeaning: Define different working widths of two subsystems
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Side-broom and side-scrub options change values
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Do not use the widest sweep path as scrub width.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Official sources publish multiple path definitions.

performanceMetrics.name: Hopper capacity
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Nominal volume, sometimes source-defined usable load
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Volume alone ignores debris density and discharge height.

performanceMetrics.name: Solution and recovery capacity
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Does not establish run time or water efficiency.

performanceMetrics.name: Area performance
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Exclude dumps, fills, turns, transport and overlap before comparison.

performanceMetrics.name: Runtime or fuel duty
performanceMetrics.reportingBoundary: Battery, fuel, settings and site dependent
performanceMetrics.comparisonCaution: Battery runtime and engine tank endurance are not equivalent metrics.
performanceMetrics.evidence: Manufacturers publish power configurations and selected runtime data.

procurementDecisions.intendedTask: Replace separate sweep and scrub passes
procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Completed debris removal and wet recovery in the actual route
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Accepting one-pass marketing without a representative trial
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturers document integrated systems but results are site-dependent.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Measure rework, hopper dumps, fills and edge work across a full shift.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Run a controlled trial with representative debris and soils.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm brushes, hopper, filter, deck, squeegee, tanks and powertrain.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Debris classification, filter system and servicing exposure
procurementDecisions.comparisonTrap: Treating a panel filter as hazardous-dust approval
procurementDecisions.evidence: Official sources document ordinary sweep dust systems.
procurementDecisions.scope: Non-hazardous use unless exact approval exists.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Specify the dust requirement before choosing the machine.
procurementDecisions.basis: Dust control and dust hazard are different boundaries.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Obtain dust classification and applicable compliance evidence.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Verify filters, seals, suppression, emptying and PPE method.

procurementDecisions.attributeToVerify: Shift duty, utilities, ventilation, emissions and service capability
procurementDecisions.evidence: Manufacturer sources publish different power options.
procurementDecisions.assessment: Select powertrain through a site utility and risk assessment.
procurementDecisions.buyerAction: Model full-shift energy or fuel demand and downtime.
procurementDecisions.engineeringCheck: Confirm battery or engine, charger or fuel system, ventilation and fire controls.

engineeringChecks.reason: Sweep, dust, scrub and recovery parts have separate configuration boundaries.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Record exact deck, hopper, filter and squeegee part numbers.

engineeringChecks.reason: Machine size and hopper discharge can constrain use.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Measure aisles, turns, doors, ramps, transport and dump point.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Manufacturers publish dimensions and hopper systems.

engineeringChecks.reason: Dry debris and wet chemistry create different exposure and disposal requirements.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Approve dust, chemical and wastewater methods.
engineeringChecks.evidence: Official systems include filtration and solution recovery.

engineeringChecks.reason: Battery and engine variants require different infrastructure and skills.
engineeringChecks.buyerAction: Confirm utilities, spare parts, training and service SLA.
